statement_en: Assume $f \in C(\mathbb{T}\to \mathbb{C})$, and the series of its Fourier coefficients converges absolutely, that is, $$\sum_{n\in \mathbb{Z}}|\widehat{f}(n)|<\infty.$$ Then the partial sums of the Fourier series of $f$ converge uniformly to $f$ itself.

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators

abbrev Torus := { z : ℂ // ‖z‖ = 1 }

theorem absoluteSummable_fourierCoefficients_uniformConvergence
    {f : Torus → ℂ} {fhat : ℤ → ℂ}
    (hf : Continuous f)
    (hcoeff : Summable (fun n : ℤ => ‖fhat n‖)) :
    TendstoUniformly
      (fun N : ℕ => fun z : Torus =>
        ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc (-(N : ℤ)) (N : ℤ), fhat n * ((z : ℂ) ^ (n : ℤ)))
      f
